text: Cross-Pixel Optical Flow Similarity (CP-FOS) is a new self-trained learning method based on optical flow similarity between two or more corresponding pixels in an image sequence. In particular, the optical flow field for each pixel in an image sequence is calculated using existing optical flow techniques. This optical flow field is then used to compute the cross-Pixel Optical Flow Similarity between the two consecutive corresponding pixels in the image sequence. This similarity measures the similarity of the motion pattern of the neighboring corresponding pixels in the image sequence, and is used to train deep neural networks. This method has the following advantages over existing self-trained methods. First, it does not rely on any external supervision, such as masks for object segmentation, or camera positions for stereo matching.
